endowment_summary: Taught chess by sister at 9, won World Under-12 Championship at 12 with 8/9 ahead of future GMs. Earned grandmaster title at 17. Exceptional early chess ability though not quite prodigy-level in the IMO-gold sense.
inherited_summary: Mother was a mining engineer and father a Russian Jewish physicist, but both lost professional jobs during the Soviet collapse, creating economic hardship. Professional family background offset by adversity.
ecosystem_summary: Sister introduced chess; GM Melikset Khachiyan lived in the family home for five years as live-in coach. Armenian chess culture and Petrosian Chess School camp provided strong ecosystem support.

endowment_summary: Started table tennis at 5, selected for PLA August 1st Team at 11, became youngest-ever Chinese national team member at 15, won World Junior Championship at 15. Exceptional early achievement in a hyper-competitive domain.
inherited_summary: Father graduated from South China University of Technology and worked for a company in Guangzhou. Middle-class family; parents were initially reluctant to let him pursue sports full-time, preferring academics.
ecosystem_summary: Chinese national table tennis pipeline — arguably the most elite sports system in the world. PLA August 1st Team at 11, Guangzhou table tennis culture, dedicated coaches who recognized and persuaded parents about his talent.

endowment_summary: Mathematical aptitude evident from school days. Completed B.Sc (Honours) in Physics by 20, MA by 21. Co-developed V-A theory of weak interactions at 25. Exceptional early achievement in theoretical physics.
inherited_summary: Born into a Syrian Christian family in Kerala. Mother was a school teacher, father a revenue inspector. Middle-class, educated family with academic orientation.
ecosystem_summary: Three formative years at TIFR under Homi Bhabha, served as scribe for Dirac's quantum mechanics lectures. Recruited by Robert Marshak for PhD at Rochester, where he formulated V-A theory within two years.

endowment_summary: Won Austrian national downhill championship at 22 and slalom titles at 25-26. Capable polyvalent skier but no particular prodigy indicators; achieved through immersion in the sport from childhood.
inherited_summary: Grew up in Obernberg am Brenner in Tyrol. No specific family wealth or domain connections mentioned beyond geographic immersion in skiing country.
ecosystem_summary: Tyrol is the heartland of Austrian alpine skiing, providing direct immersion from an early age. Trained with Sportverein Tirol and rose through the Austrian skiing pipeline, winning first World Cup race ever held in 1967.

endowment_summary: Prolific copywriter who wrote 300+ ads in his first year. No film school or prodigy indicators; built creative skills through sheer volume of advertising work. Capable and driven but not exceptional early cognitive ability.
inherited_summary: Working-class family on a council estate in Islington. Father was a house painter, mother a dressmaker. No film industry connections. Father was actively discouraging of his creative endeavors.
ecosystem_summary: London advertising scene of the 1960s provided a creative frontier without class barriers. Met David Puttnam and Alan Marshall at Collett Dickenson Pearce, forming a high-trust peer team that later produced his films.

endowment_summary: Left school at 13 to work as a construction laborer. No cognitive prodigy indicators; success driven by physical fitness, leadership in combat, and opportunistic timing rather than exceptional early ability.
inherited_summary: Born into an impoverished peasant family in Kerman Province. Father was a landless peasant with government debt. Left school at 13 to work construction to repay father's debts. Active economic disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: The 1979 Islamic Revolution was a massive structural wave that created the IRGC, which he joined at 22. The Iran-Iraq War provided frontline combat immersion that rapidly accelerated his military career.

endowment_summary: Started hockey at 13 at CSKA Moscow. Capable goaltender who won multiple World Championship golds and Olympic gold, but was a backup for most of his national team career. Above average but not prodigy-level.
inherited_summary: From a working-class Moscow family. No specific family wealth or domain connections mentioned. Entered the CSKA system through neighborhood proximity.
ecosystem_summary: Trained under legendary coach Anatoly Tarasov at CSKA Moscow from 1958 — the Soviet hockey system was a once-in-a-generation elite pipeline. Later joined Spartak Moscow and the Soviet national team, winning 5 World Championship golds.

endowment_summary: Uncle recognized early facility for drawing and provided first lessons. Entered the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando at 14. Above-average early ability with sustained mentorship, but not a prodigy in the self-taught sense.
inherited_summary: Born to a well-to-do farming family in Tomelloso. His uncle, painter Antonio López Torres, identified his talent and convinced his parents to send him to Madrid at 13. Family-domain connection through uncle was pivotal.
ecosystem_summary: Uncle provided sustained mentorship in painting from life. Entered prestigious Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando at 14, where he met his peer group of New Spanish Realists (Lucio Muñoz, Isabel Quintanilla, etc.).

endowment_summary: Built an extensive amateur career (46 fights, one loss) before turning professional at 21. Natural physical talent and toughness, but no particular prodigy indicators — success came through volume of fights and physical attributes.
inherited_summary: Born to Italian immigrant parents in working-class Buenos Aires. Father was a tram driver, mother an ironer. Seventh of nine children. Active economic disadvantage as working-class immigrants.
ecosystem_summary: Buenos Aires boxing scene provided amateur grounding. Moved to NYC under manager Marvin Goldberg, fighting at Madison Square Garden. Some access to the boxing ecosystem but no elite pipeline or notable mentor.

endowment_summary: Learned to drive trucks at 6, natural talent for racing. Saved for an MG TF and began racing at 21. Capable and determined but not a prodigy — success came through early domain exposure and mechanical aptitude.
inherited_summary: Son of WWII Victoria Cross winner Clive Hulme, who ran a trucking business. Father bought him an MG TF and later an MGA. Upper-middle-class rural context with direct access to vehicles and mechanical skills.
ecosystem_summary: Selected for the prestigious New Zealand Driver to Europe scholarship in 1960. Connected with Jack Brabham as mechanic and driver, and with Bruce McLaren in London. Elite mentor and scholarship program at the right time.

endowment_summary: Driving cars at 10 on frozen lakes, co-driving for father at 12, took second place in first rally at 18. Exceptional early domain achievement through direct immersion from a very young age.
inherited_summary: Father was a local rally competitor and driving school owner. Uncle owned a car garage where Stig drove customers' cars on frozen lakes. Direct family-domain immersion in motorsport from age 10.
ecosystem_summary: Swedish rally ecosystem with frozen lake practice conditions. Saab factory support from 1965, providing engines, gearboxes, and eventually full works team status. Frontier geography for winter rallying.

endowment_summary: Rejected by Coventry and Doncaster for being too small. Built himself through relentless Sunday league football and weight training. Capable and driven but not a prodigy — success came through determination and the right break.
inherited_summary: Born to a coal-mining family in Armthorpe, Yorkshire. Father was a miner who had served in Burma. Working-class background with no football connections. Left school with two O-Levels.
ecosystem_summary: Signed by Scunthorpe United as apprentice at 15. Bill Shankly signed him for Liverpool at 20 for £35,000, forming a formidable strike partnership with John Toshack. Elite institution under a legendary manager.

endowment_summary: Hit by furniture truck at 13, channeled into swimming. Won 10 AAU titles in high school, two Olympic golds at 21. Exceptional achievement driven by extraordinary work ethic and mega-mileage training pioneer approach.
inherited_summary: Son of a truck driver. Working-class family that moved from Iowa to Sacramento. No particular financial or domain advantages; swimming was chosen due to injury constraints.
ecosystem_summary: Arden Hills Swim Club under Hall of Fame coach Sherm Chavoor, whose revolutionary over-distance training matched Burton's work ethic. Later swam at UCLA under Hall of Fame coach Bob Horn. Elite coaching pipeline.

endowment_summary: Developed passion for acting at prep school at age 9. Won RADA scholarship in 1960. Above-average early ability and drive, but not a prodigy — success came through institutional pipeline and key casting.
inherited_summary: Father was an Anglican clergyman (formerly a mathematician), mother a former actress who became a draughtsman. Middle-class upbringing with access to prep school. Mother's brief acting career provided some domain proximity.
ecosystem_summary: Prep school theatre at St Michael's in Kent provided early acting exposure. RADA scholarship was the key institutional pipeline for British acting. Fred Zinnemann cast him in A Man for All Seasons after seeing his stage work.

endowment_summary: Self-taught motorcycle racer who won 11 French national titles in three years through sheer talent and repetition. Exceptional achievement with no coaching, mentor, or elite pipeline — entirely self-created.
inherited_summary: Working-class Parisian family. Father owned a butcher shop. No motorsport connections or financial support. Started racing because he couldn't afford car racing.
ecosystem_summary: No mentor, no elite pipeline, no family support. Entirely self-taught from age 18. The only ecosystem factor was access to French national motorcycle racing competitions. No meaningful ecosystem advantage.

endowment_summary: Father commissioned a garden pavilion at age 13-14, his first built project. Completed four houses and opened a practice before even graduating at 21. Exceptional early achievement with direct built-work experience as a teenager.
inherited_summary: Bourgeois Roman Catholic family in Matosinhos. Father was an engineer and teacher who commissioned his first project. Family background enabled education at Porto Fine Arts School from age 16.
ecosystem_summary: Porto School of Architecture provided elite training. Collaborated with Fernando Távora (1955-58), a notable mentor. The Porto School became one of the most influential architectural traditions in Europe.

endowment_summary: Showed immediate natural talent, reaching Swedish Rally podium within three years of starting at 19. Capable and talented but not a prodigy — success came through early exposure and natural aptitude.
inherited_summary: Father was a local rally competitor who took him to watch rallies from age 7-8. Farming family in Rimbo, Sweden. Modest family-domain exposure to rallying but no significant wealth or connections.
ecosystem_summary: Swedish rally ecosystem provided early immersion. VW importer sponsorship led to Porsche factory support. Won Swedish Rally Championship in 1967 with Porsche 911, then Monte Carlo Rally for Porsche factory team in 1969.

endowment_summary: Scouted at age 8 by Cuban state coaches based on physical attributes. World Wrestling Champion at 22, Olympic silver at 23. Physical prodigy with exceptional natural athletic ability identified and developed from childhood.
inherited_summary: Father was on the Cuban national boxing team. Half-brother Yoan Pablo Hernandez became world boxing champion. Family-domain advantage in combat sports with direct genetic and cultural transmission.
ecosystem_summary: Cuban state sports system — scouted at 8, placed in specialist wrestling school. The Cuban combat sports pipeline is arguably once-in-a-generation elite, producing systematic Olympic champions in wrestling and boxing.

endowment_summary: Playing piano at 3, choir at 6, flute at 11. Won scholarship to Royal Academy of Music at 17. Exceptional early musical ability across multiple instruments and voice, though left before completing her degree.
inherited_summary: Working-class Aberdeen household. Father was a shipyard worker/welder, mother a cook. No musical family background or financial advantages. Teachers were concerned she would 'end up in a factory.'
ecosystem_summary: Royal Academy of Music scholarship provided elite classical training. Met Dave Stewart in London, forming a high-trust peer partnership (The Tourists, then Eurythmics). New wave timing was perfect for their synth-pop direction.

endowment_summary: Exceptional climbing ability from the start of his cycling career. Progressed through amateur categories with Girobio finishes of 3rd, 2nd, and 1st (1990-1992). Rare domain-specific climbing talent evident early.
inherited_summary: Working-class family in Cesenatico. Father was an engineer, mother a chambermaid. No cycling family background or financial advantages. Grandfather helped buy his first racing bike.
ecosystem_summary: Joined local Fausto Coppi cycling club of Cesenatico at 11 after a neighbor's suggestion. Good local club environment but not an elite pipeline or notable mentor. Italian cycling culture provided general support.

endowment_summary: Top scorer in Kanto university league for four consecutive years at Waseda. Won Emperor's Cup twice (last time a university team won). Exceptional achievement in Japanese university football, debuting for national team at 20.
inherited_summary: Born in Kyoto, attended Yamashiro High School then Waseda University School of Commerce. Middle-class family with access to elite university education. No specific football family background mentioned.
ecosystem_summary: Waseda University provided an elite academic-athletic pipeline. National team selection at 20, Tokyo Olympics at 20, Mexico City Olympics at 24. Dettmar Cramer (German coach of Japan team) was a key mentor figure.

endowment_summary: Began competing at 16, won first title at 20, reached French Open final at 23. Capable clay-court specialist with above-average talent, but not a prodigy — developed through local club tennis and tournament repetition.
inherited_summary: Born on island of Korčula, raised in Split from age one month. Parents Ivo and Katica. No specific family wealth or tennis connections mentioned. Working-to-middle-class background.
ecosystem_summary: Split tennis club at Firule produced multiple tennis stars including Nikola Pilić, who was a local role model. Yugoslav tennis center provided competition access. Good local tennis environment but not an elite academy.

endowment_summary: Olympic gold at 14 years and 41 days — youngest-ever female Olympic swimming champion. International debut at 13. Prodigy-level ability with ideal physique for backstroke, recognized and developed from age 4.
inherited_summary: Born in Budapest. No specific family wealth or swimming background mentioned. Middle-class Hungarian family. No particular inherited advantage or disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Structured coaching pipeline: Miklós Kiss (age 4-5), György Turi (age 6-12), then László Kiss — Hungarian national team coach from age 12. Budapesti Spartacus SC. Sustained, high-quality individualized coaching from a young age.

endowment_summary: Started fencing early, won World Championship team gold at 22 and Olympic team bronze at 23. Capable fencer who benefited from the Soviet system, but no particular prodigy indicators or individual distinction at young age.
inherited_summary: Born to Russian mother and Cuban father in Almaty, Kazakhstan. No specific family wealth or fencing connections mentioned. Multicultural background but no domain advantage.
ecosystem_summary: Soviet fencing pipeline, training at Dynamo Tallinn from 1984. The Soviet sports system provided elite coaching, facilities, and competition access. World Championship and Olympic team medals followed from system access.

endowment_summary: Belgian junior cyclo-cross champion before converting to road racing. Capable and talented with above-average early results, but not a prodigy — developed through cyclo-cross background and Flemish cycling culture.
inherited_summary: Father Eddy had been a professional cyclist for two seasons (teammate of Frans Verbeeck). Grew up in Gistel, West Flanders — heartland of Flemish cycling. Family-domain connection through father's professional cycling career.
ecosystem_summary: Flemish cycling culture in West Flanders is one of the world's premier cycling regions. Zeemeeuw Oostende club, cyclo-cross junior champion. Turned professional with ADR team alongside Greg LeMond at 22.

endowment_summary: Enrolled at Barnamúsíkskóli music school at 6 studying piano and flute. Radio broadcast at 11 led to self-titled album at 11, including an original instrumental composition. Exceptional early musical ability and creative output.
inherited_summary: Stepfather Sævar Árnason was a guitarist in the band Pops, providing a musical household. Mother was an activist, father an electrician. Parents divorced early; raised in a commune. Modest musical family advantage through stepfather.
ecosystem_summary: Barnamúsíkskóli music school provided specialized classical training from age 6. Icelandic post-punk scene provided creative peer environment. KUKL and the Sugarcubes were part of a unique Icelandic creative movement.

endowment_summary: Self-trained initially using physical labor as conditioning. World Allround Champion at 21 — first Soviet male to win. Exceptional achievement through natural talent and self-created training methods despite wartime adversity.
inherited_summary: Father lost during WWII when Oleg was 10. Grew up in war-torn Kharkiv under Nazi occupation with hunger and fear. Mother was a cycling champion but family was impoverished. Active disadvantage from war and poverty.
ecosystem_summary: Dynamo sports society provided entry to formal coaching under V. Zhelubovsky and K. Kudryavtsev. The Soviet sports system then provided elite-level support. Graduated from Kharkiv Fire Technical School before entering the sports pipeline.

endowment_summary: Learned chess at age 2, knew all rules by 3. European Youth champion at 6. Won multiple European and World Youth Championships. IM at 17, GM at 21. Prodigy-level ability with trajectory-changing early achievement.
inherited_summary: Both parents are professional chess coaches who taught at the Lviv State Institute of Physical Culture. Homeschooled to maximize chess training time. Sister Mariya also became GM and Women's World Champion. Rare, trajectory-changing family-domain advantage.
ecosystem_summary: Lviv has a strong chess tradition with many GMs. Coached by Roman Kozel and GM Orest Gritsak. Slovenian federation support from age 14. Strong chess culture and coaching, though the family-domain advantage was the primary driver.

endowment_summary: Multi-sport talent initially (volleyball, gymnastics) before being steered to athletics. Won first national long jump title at 23. Capable athlete with perseverance, but not a prodigy — success came through system support and determination.
inherited_summary: Lost mother at age 5, raised by grandparents. Family fled as refugees to Bucharest during WWII. Active disadvantage from orphanhood, war displacement, and poverty.
ecosystem_summary: Discovered by coach Ion Vintilă at a school competition. Steaua Bucharest (army club) and the Romanian sports system provided elite coaching under Ion Soter. Nine consecutive national titles followed from institutional support.

endowment_summary: Learned guitar at 12 from a Bert Weedon manual, gigging by 15. Prolific songwriter and multi-instrumentalist. Capable and driven with early start, but not a prodigy — built skills through repetition and the London rock scene.
inherited_summary: Born in Plumstead, London, moved to Stevenage with family. No particular musical family background mentioned. Father was re-assigned to Stevenage for work. Working-to-middle-class family.
ecosystem_summary: London rock scene of the 1960s provided structural momentum. Formed The Gods at 19 with future stars Mick Taylor (Rolling Stones) and Greg Lake (King Crimson, ELP). Marquee club residency. Signed to EMI/Columbia Records.

endowment_summary: No particular cognitive or creative prodigy indicators. Success driven primarily by physical beauty and pageant pipeline. Average ability in traditional cognitive/creative domains.
inherited_summary: Father Enzo Bolocco was a businessman who owned Chilemotores (Ford partnership) and Televisores Bolocco. Upper-middle-class family. Attended private Santiago College. Significant financial and social advantages.
ecosystem_summary: Chilean pageant pipeline and Miss Universe system. Private school education provided poise and social skills. No particular elite institutional or mentor advantage beyond the pageant system itself.

endowment_summary: Medaled in all five events at World Junior Championships at 19. Exceptional all-discipline alpine skiing talent. World Champion in combined at 22. Rare multi-discipline ability evident from junior level.
inherited_summary: Father built a 40-yard slalom slope for neighborhood kids. Supportive family in Siggerud, Norway. No significant wealth but active parental support for skiing development.
ecosystem_summary: Norwegian alpine skiing culture. First coach was Finn Aamodt, father of friend and future champion Kjetil André Aamodt — providing both elite coaching and a peer-level rival. National team pipeline from age 14.

endowment_summary: No cognitive or creative prodigy indicators. Career launched by exceptional physical beauty (Miss Sweden at 18). Reportedly skipped drama lessons at Universal. No meaningful advantage in learning speed or creativity.
inherited_summary: Father was a harbour master/doctor (sources vary). Sixth of eight children in Malmö, Sweden. Middle-class family. No film industry connections but respectable professional background.
ecosystem_summary: Miss Sweden title led to Universal Studios starlet contract with training in drama, elocution, dancing, and fencing. Hollywood studio system of the 1950s provided the pipeline, though she reportedly didn't take full advantage of training.

endowment_summary: No cognitive or creative prodigy indicators. Scouted at 15 at a bus stop for physical beauty. Success driven by physical appearance and the Venezuelan pageant system. No meaningful advantage in learning speed or creativity.
inherited_summary: Born in Caracas to Willy Mendoza and María Moncada. No specific family wealth or connections mentioned. Working-to-middle-class background. Experienced kidnapping in Venezuela, showing resilience.
ecosystem_summary: Elite Model Management signing at 15 after Elite Model Look competition. Venezuelan pageant system — the world's most dominant pageant pipeline — and Miss Venezuela organization. International modeling career provided poise and exposure.

endowment_summary: Started piano at 6 learning from father. Organist and choirmaster at 14. Became one of London's most in-demand session musicians and arrangers by 18. Exceptional early musical achievement across multiple instruments and arranging.
inherited_summary: Father was a professional big-band pianist and arranger (Ambrose and his Orchestra). Mother also worked in music business. Family performed together as vaudeville act. Rare, trajectory-changing family-domain advantage with both parents in music.
ecosystem_summary: London 1960s session musician pipeline provided hundreds of recording opportunities with major artists. Boarding school music education at Christ's College. Connected with Jet Harris of The Shadows at 17. Co-founded Led Zeppelin with Jimmy Page at 22.

endowment_summary: Joined local club Kurikan Ryhti before starting school. Multi-sport talent (orienteering, hammer throw). Capable cross-country skier with exceptional endurance, but not a prodigy — developed through Finnish skiing tradition and physical attributes.
inherited_summary: Born in Kurikka, Finland. No specific family wealth or skiing connections mentioned. Working-class background in rural Finland. No particular inherited advantage or disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Finnish cross-country skiing tradition is one of the world's deepest. Kurikan Ryhti local club provided early training. Finnish national team pipeline. Good national skiing culture but no elite mentor or special institutional access mentioned.

endowment_summary: Skipped two years of elementary school. Master's degree at 19, PhD at 24 with groundbreaking thesis published in Acta Mathematica. Fields Medal winner. Prodigy-level mathematical ability with trajectory-changing early achievement.
inherited_summary: Father was a school teacher in Mjällby, Blekinge. Middle-class, educated family. Five children. No particular wealth but stable academic household that valued education.
ecosystem_summary: Gymnasium teacher Nils Erik Fremberg, a Lund University docent and student of Marcel Riesz, taught him university-level mathematics while still in secondary school. Marcel Riesz became his mentor at Lund University. Elite mentor and university pipeline.

endowment_summary: Started boxing at 14, won Pan American Games gold at 18 and Olympic gold at 19. Rapid rise but late start — capable and talented, not a prodigy. Success driven by the Cuban boxing system's intensity and his natural aptitude.
inherited_summary: From Santiago de Cuba. No specific family wealth or boxing connections mentioned. Inspired by local boxers from Santiago de Cuba. Working-class background.
ecosystem_summary: Cuban state-sponsored amateur boxing system — arguably once-in-a-generation elite for amateur boxing. National team selection provided elite training, facilities, and competition. Won Olympic gold at 19, knocking out defending champion Manfred Wolke.

endowment_summary: Began skiing at 5, won first national competition at 8. Won first World Cup race at 18, eventually accumulating 86 World Cup wins — most by any male alpine skier. Exceptional early achievement with technical mastery from childhood.
inherited_summary: From small village Joesjö in Lapland. Father coached him until 13. Family moved to Tärnaby when he was 4. No significant wealth but supportive family in a skiing-focused community.
ecosystem_summary: Tärnaby, a small Swedish village that produced multiple elite skiers including Stig Strand. Swedish junior national team at 13. Italian coach Hermann Nogler spotted and nurtured his talent. Frontier geography with unique skiing community.

endowment_summary: Ring debut at 13, Junior World champion at 18, first senior World Championship gold at 19. Exceptional early achievement in boxing, with 6 consecutive World Championship titles. Natural talent developed by the Cuban system.
inherited_summary: Born in San Vicente, Guantánamo Province, Cuba. No specific family wealth or boxing connections mentioned. Working-class rural background. Inspired by Teófilo Stevenson rather than family.
ecosystem_summary: Cuban state-sponsored amateur boxing system — once-in-a-generation elite pipeline. Inspired and mentored by Teófilo Stevenson, three-time Olympic champion, with whom he had a father-son relationship. Six consecutive World Championship titles.

endowment_summary: Began creating manga around 12, publishing doujinshi and contributing to magazines. First professional work published at 16. Tezuka was so impressed he sent a telegraph inviting him as assistant. Exceptional early achievement recognized by the master.
inherited_summary: Father was a local government official who became chairman of the Board of Education. Family ran a general goods store. Middle-class, educated family. Father was strict but supportive enough to allow the Tokyo move.
ecosystem_summary: Tokiwa-so was a once-in-a-generation peer environment — the legendary manga incubator where Tezuka, Fujiko F. Fujio, Akatsuka Fujio, and others lived and worked. Tezuka's direct mentorship on Astro Boy. Manga Shōnen contest provided early publication platform.

endowment_summary: Started table tennis at 8, European Youth champion at 13, Hungarian national champion at 16, World Championship gold at 17. Exceptional early achievement despite being initially rejected as talentless by a coach.
inherited_summary: Poor family in Budapest. Father was a junk dealer, mother a newspaper deliverer. Fourth child, nearly not born. Two older sisters were first-division table tennis players, providing family-domain exposure despite poverty.
ecosystem_summary: Older brother Józsi provided intense daily training at Postás SE, effectively serving as his coach. Hungarian table tennis pipeline. World Championship doubles gold at 17 with István Jónyer. Sibling-coach relationship was pivotal.

endowment_summary: Multi-sport talent (football, basketball, boxing) in youth. Debuted in Primera División at 21. Capable and versatile athlete, but not a football prodigy — developed relatively late after economic necessity pushed him to professional football.
inherited_summary: Father Antonio played for Rosario Central in the amateur era and transmitted football passion. Father died of cancer in 1955 when Menotti was 16, creating economic hardship. Father's football background offset by his death and resulting poverty.
ecosystem_summary: Rosario football culture provided immersion. Played for pay in the Carcarañense League before being scouted by Rosario Central. Good local football environment but no elite academy or notable mentor in his early development.

endowment_summary: Began ballet at 9 at School of the National Ballet Prague. Made first choreographic attempts at Prague Conservatory. Received scholarship to Royal Ballet School at 20. Exceptional early achievement with choreographic debut at 23.
inherited_summary: Father was a banker who became director of the largest savings bank in Czechoslovakia. Mother was a dancer-child prodigy who sold out theaters at age 10. Upper-middle-class family with direct dance-domain connection through mother.
ecosystem_summary: Prague Conservatory under mentor Zora Šemberová (world-first interpreter of Juliet in Prokofiev's ballet). Royal Ballet School scholarship in London. John Cranko at Stuttgart Ballet provided choreographic opportunities. Once-in-a-generation institutional pipeline.

endowment_summary: Won prestigious Soen Prize for fashion design at 21 while still a student. One of the first male students at Bunka Fashion College. Designed up to 40 outfits per month at Sanai department store. Exceptional early achievement in fashion.
inherited_summary: Family ran a hotel in Himeji. One of seven children. Father died during his first year at university, creating financial pressure. Middle-class family business background with some hardship from father's death.
ecosystem_summary: Bunka Fashion College was Japan's premier fashion education institution. Graduating class ('Flowering Ninth Class') included Junko Koshino and Mitsuhiro Matsuda. Sanai department store provided professional experience. Paris fashion scene access from 1964.

endowment_summary: Started cycling at 18 for rehabilitation after skiing accident. Turned professional at 23, won Paris-Nice and finished 2nd in Vuelta at 25. Capable with rapid rise but late start — not a prodigy, developed through determination and natural endurance.
inherited_summary: Swiss father and Dutch mother in Wil, Switzerland. Father bought cycling equipment to encourage him after the skiing accident. Middle-class, supportive family. No cycling family background.
ecosystem_summary: Swiss cycling culture provided general support. ONCE team under Manolo Saiz provided professional platform. Good professional team environment but no elite mentor or special institutional access in early development.

endowment_summary: Started handball at 8, joined FC Barcelona youth system at 14, reached senior team at 18. Capable goalkeeper with above-average ability, but not a prodigy — success driven by the extraordinary FC Barcelona pipeline and longevity.
inherited_summary: Born in Barcelona. Older brother Jaume played handball, introducing him to the sport. Middle-class family in Barcelona. Family-domain exposure through brother but no significant wealth or professional connections.
ecosystem_summary: FC Barcelona youth system and senior team — one of the most elite club pipelines in handball history, winning 7 European Cups during his tenure. Valero Rivera convinced him to join. 26-year career at one club. Once-in-a-generation elite club environment.

endowment_summary: Relatively unknown cyclist who won the 1969 World Championship as a late replacement. Good sprinter with some Tour de France stage podiums, but no particular prodigy indicators or exceptional early ability. Average ability that peaked in one race.
inherited_summary: Born in Alkmaar, Netherlands. No specific family wealth or cycling connections mentioned. Working-class background. Former interior decorator. No particular inherited advantage or disadvantage.
ecosystem_summary: Dutch cycling culture provided general support. DTS Zaandam club, then Willem II Gazelle professional team. Good cycling culture but no elite mentor or special institutional access. Won World Championship largely through circumstance (late selection, Merckx boycott).

endowment_summary: Began gymnastics at 6, invited to elite training at 15. Olympic team gold at 21 with Unified Team. Capable gymnast who benefited from the Soviet system, but no particular prodigy indicators or exceptional individual distinction at young age.
inherited_summary: Born in Dushanbe, Tajik SSR to Tajik father and Ukrainian mother. Parents worked at a silk factory. Working-class family. No gymnastics family background. Parents supported his training but had no domain connections.
ecosystem_summary: Soviet gymnastics system — once-in-a-generation elite pipeline. Invited to Club Dynamo camp in Moscow at 10, then Ukrainian National Center in Kyiv at 15 with frequent Moscow trips. Unified Team won 20 medals at 1992 Olympics. Legendary system.

endowment_summary: No cognitive or creative prodigy indicators. Career driven by physical attractiveness. No evidence of exceptional learning speed, reasoning, or domain aptitude. Entered adult film industry at 23 with no prior training or notable ability.
inherited_summary: Born in Tiszalök, Hungary. No family background information available — no evidence of wealth, domain connections, or significant advantages. Working-class background in rural Hungary.
ecosystem_summary: Italian and German adult film markets of the early 1990s provided the industry context. No elite pipeline, mentor, or institutional access. Discovered through a casting agency. No meaningful ecosystem advantage.
